findings.text: Upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet reaches 14.9% [OSWorld](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07972) screenshot-only success (22% with up to 50 steps), far below the reported 72.4% human rate.

source.quote: While this represents a significant advancement over previous results, it remains well below human performance of 72.36%, indicating substantial room for future improvement in this domain.

findings.text: Computer-use Trust & Safety red-teaming flagged scaled account creation, content distribution, age-assurance bypass, and abusive form filling, but none as imminent.

source.quote: These include: scaled account creation; scaled content distribution; age assurance bypass; and abusive form filling.

findings.text: Both models struggled with nuanced harmful requests framed as fiction, roleplaying, or artistic content despite overall harm-rate improvements.

source.quote: identified that both models struggled with nuanced requests or those framed as fiction, roleplaying, or artistic content.

findings.text: Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) testing found stronger chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN), cyber, and autonomy-relevant capabilities than prior models, still below AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3).

source.quote: However, we observed stronger capabilities across all domains. In CBRN domains, the model demonstrated improved performance on both knowledge retrieval and skills as-

findings.text: Anthropic judged current threat models still adequate for nascent computer use at this capability level across CBRN, cyber, and autonomy.

source.quote: we are confident that our current threat models or evaluations adequately capture the risks of computer use.

findings.text: Models did not trigger the full RSP evaluation protocol, but Anthropic says it will keep testing frontier models regularly.
